summary: Neo falls asleep in front of his PC and wakes to a message typing itself on the screen: 'Wake up, Neo.' His keystrokes only produce single letters, and the machine keeps writing on its own until it tells him 'The Matrix has you,' then 'Follow the white rabbit,' then 'Knock, knock, Neo.' At that last message someone actually knocks on his door; when he looks back the screen is blank. He opens the door with the chain still on and deals with Choi, a young man who has come with friends to buy an illegal computer disk. Neo retrieves a disk hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations, takes Choi's two grand, and hands over the disk while Choi insists 'This never happened. You don't exist.' The odd feeling makes Neo ask whether they've ever been unsure if they're awake or still dreaming. Choi jokes it's mescaline and suggests Neo needs to 'unplug,' then asks Dujour whether they should take him along. Dujour urges him to come, and Neo notices a small white rabbit pinned to her jacket. The room tilts, and he agrees to go with them.

what_changes.before: Asleep and oblivious, woken by an ordinary-looking computer that behaves strangely.
what_changes.after: Told by the machine itself that larger forces know and are directing him, leaving him 'unable to explain what just happened.'
what_changes.evidence: He stops and stares at the four words on the screen: "The Matrix has you."

what_changes.before: He refuses to go out with Choi's group, saying 'I can't. I have to work tomorrow.'
what_changes.after: After seeing the white rabbit on Dujour's jacket, he reverses himself and agrees to go.
what_changes.evidence: A small white rabbit.  The ROOM TILTS. NEO Yeah, yeah. Sure, I'll go.

what_changes.before: A customer arriving late to make an illicit purchase from Neo.
what_changes.after: Grateful and reverent toward Neo once he hands over the illegal disk, calling him his savior.
what_changes.evidence: Opening the door, he hands the disk to Choi. CHOI Hallelujah!  You are my Savior, man!

event_hint.one_line: A mysterious self-typing message lures Neo toward a white-rabbit signal, then Choi's drug-buying visit gives him a reason to follow it.

objects_that_matter: the PC screen and its self-typed messages
the door with its series of locks and chain
Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations, hollowed out to hide disks
uncertain: Whether the computer messages are a real external signal or a dream/hallucination.
What the illegal software on the disk does.
Where Choi and his group are taking Neo or what 'unplug' will involve.

minds.wants: To re-establish that his world is ordinary and under his control after the screen told him otherwise.
minds.feels: A vertiginous 'unrealness' — the boundary between awake and dreaming has come unglued, and something is directing him without his consent.
minds.shows: A cool, transactional dealer who keeps the chain on the door and treats the visitors as a routine sale.
minds.basis: The four words 'The Matrix has you' freeze him; he then asks Choi whether he's ever been unsure if he's awake or dreaming, and can't explain what happened. His reversal to 'Sure, I'll go' only after the room tilts at the rabbit pin shows the pull is not rational.

believes_about.belief: Choi is just a stoned customer who can laugh off the weirdness as mescaline.
believes_about.wrong_because: Choi's 'You don't exist' is truer than he means, and Neo's own experience is not a drug; Neo treats him as a normalcy-anchor who actually can't explain anything to him.

believes_about.belief: It is a coincidence or a party detail that happens to echo the screen's command.
believes_about.wrong_because: It is the planted signal meant to lure him; he reads it as a sign but not yet as a trap, and does not know Trinity (from the preceding scenes) is the one steering him.

minds.wants: To get the illegal disk and get out, while keeping the exchange deniable.
minds.feels: A giddy, reverent dependence on Neo as his source of escape ('my savior,' 'personal Jesus'), mixed with street wariness about being caught.
minds.shows: A wisecracking 'droog' who jokes about mescaline and insists 'This never happened. You don't exist' — turning real danger into a punchline.
minds.basis: His 'Hallelujah!' outburst on receiving the disk, and his rehearsed 'This never happened' line. He also notices Neo going pale and asks if something's wrong.

believes_about.belief: Neo is a freaked-out dealer who needs to 'unplug' and get laid, not someone being genuinely hunted.
believes_about.wrong_because: From the events just before, Agents already have Neo's name and a search is running; Choi's flippancy is exactly the blindness of the world Neo is about to lose.

believes_about.belief: It is just contraband software that will get him in trouble if caught.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has no idea it is a thread in the same operation that is tracking Neo; he thinks the danger is legal, not existential.

minds.wants: To pull Neo out of his apartment and into the night with them.
minds.feels: A light, inviting confidence; she is the social instrument of a plan she doesn't fully comprehend.
minds.shows: Warm persuasion — 'Come on. It'll be fun. I promise' — and an open body that lets him notice the pins and the rabbit.
minds.basis: She answers Choi's 'should we take him' with 'Definitely,' then directly coaxes him past his 'I have to work tomorrow' refusal.

believes_about.belief: He is a shy guy who needs convincing to have a good time.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is being summoned, not invited; her 'fun' is the cover for a signal that has already reached him through the machine.

connects_back: The Agents naming 'Neo' as their target and launching a search in the scene just before (sc-011) is the real pressure underneath Neo's 'unrealness,' though he cannot yet name it.
The self-typing messages ('Wake up, Neo,' 'Follow the white rabbit') are the same remote-access intrusion Trinity was running before her escape, now landing directly on Neo.
The white rabbit pin pays off the screen's 'Follow the white rabbit,' converting a digital command into a physical lure.
sets_up: Neo leaving with the group makes the club encounter with Trinity possible, where he learns she hacked his computer and is looking for Morpheus.
The 'awake or dreaming' question and 'unplug' plant the exact terms Trinity and Morpheus will later use to recruit him (ev-002, ev-006).
His willingness to follow a signal he can't explain establishes the pull that will eventually make him take the red pill and be unplugged (ev-006).
dramatic_function: It is the threshold scene that turns an abstract summons into a physical departure: the machine's message, a street-level errand, and a planted symbol converge to break Neo's ordinary world and set him moving toward the people who are hunting and saving him at once.
